ХуОо фаміІнґ ксін да.

111-8

From edge to edge The hall is packed, And I sing, Expecting no praise. Oh, in the meadow The red guelder-rose… I forgot my friends, Forgot my wife. All movement froze, Dead silence came — The spirit sings, The soul went numb.

110-9

Friends — The filling of lack. In the streak of failures — The pledge of luck. When you lack — they give, Offer a shoulder. They carry the weak, Blow on wounds when they burn. The egoist craves to take, All serve him. But are you ready to give? Or do they befriend only for you?

109-9

We are cool — We feed the whole world, Without us they are nothing. But what about us? Do we not need Their help, or what? Everyone needs greatness, Alpha-male status. You spread only for your own glory Without edge or end. Widows and orphans wait For you to care for them too. But sensing the smell of mercy, Arrogance rises from them as well.

108-8

And I about God Would like to speak. As if I knew Him, But to declare That to the level of everything — I would not yet presume. The womb has not yet opened For the birth of the soul. A heel pushes through, Verses help. And growth is lacking To press on the walls, To come out into the open From the Earth-woman. To finally say: The Mother allowed To know the Father.

107-7

The most important word, When ready, Dies with the samurai. Not the emperor's servant, But God's, Receives the Word And the road of truth. Honor Is with him, And death Brings him home.

106-9

In the painting It turns out better. For life in routine Is harder and more complex. The artist comprehended, Filtered, The most important concisely Laid in paints. He sifted the chaff, Removed wrinkles, Where needed, strengthened, Where needed — hid.

105-9

The idea of the black man Will be needed by the white too. They ask the left one, When the right cannot. Christ or Buddha Taught truths. I won't argue — They led to heaven. About Moses' laws Both spoke. Only the bows They made differently.

104-2

Do not argue with the evil one, When he takes your shirt. But allow no one To dishonor your daughter. Do not listen to advice To set up your neighbor. Fear betrayal like fire, Lest you help evil. Be ready for sacrifice, Give away your own — Prepare to die, But save the innocent.

103-9

Why the itch To change others? Why do their bolts Strip my niches? Their threading Is not right, Though it fits everyone. It's my pipe, They say, that harms. Crumpled and chipped, Torn and full of holes. Of interest to no one, It should be replaced… …But it is unsurpassed. Perfect for me.

102-8

Premonitions Don't have to come true. At times words Are allowed to err. Seeking truth — Sort through options With pure intentions. Diamonds in the trash. You'll get tangled in mistakes, But find the truth And never thank it enough For the saving advice.

101-4

Is it better in fascist shit Than in a democratic war? Will the slave and the serf Easily escape death, Staying alive, Smoldering and decaying, Paying tribute To the "elder brother"? Laying the bed For the henchman in your own house, Besides unpaid labor Also going to his wars for him?

100-9

You may envy The old emigration, Advise others Dissident actions. But the tragedy of resettlement Is not only in nostalgia. It lies in being transferred Into foreign conditions. Don't judge the driven one Who preserved his life — He ran too far From the long-suffering one.

99-9

Sick, Chained to the bed. Frail, Forgotten by all. So that he Would remember himself, Hearing the ringing, He counted. What he stumbled on, Where he sinned, What he shed, How he lived.

98-7

You don't keep up... Where to get That time? Do you even know? What you spend it on? Which track you've chosen, What to achieve? Work… Work... But what for? In worries — Vanity; Glory in follies; In haste — Squandered to the wind. Stop and think. You'll save your strength. Like a wise man, Having driven away doubt, You'll approach the grave.

97-7

The last?… Not at all. In truth, the first. In truth, That copper coin Will surpass them all. Just arrived — And immediately buys. Gave himself and again — Trades and schemes. At the bottom of the purse, not so fertile; The last receives first. The successful restless one — Clear the road for the stubborn!

96-6

They said we have no precipitation; Once I believed it myself. Winter passed without snOw, And in summer it didn't scOrch beyond measure. Something drizzled In autumn and spring, But can you call that Rain? We knew no grief, Without a bag or with a bAg — In rest and in labor, You live day by day. We convinced Ourselves and those around: Life is not hEll, But a granted paradise. We took what we wanted, Didn't notice the pain… But having gone far, We understood, you and I: In downpour or in heat, Whether cool or warm — Return home.

95-7

A playground of blood, The center of the universe, A dispute in the word — Not even a whisper remained. An echo of history, Distorted by statistics, A trampled sprout, Tormented in the bud. Born for eternity, Deprived of life. Not without the Creator's cunning Sent into eternity. (Abel)

94-9

Covering the sick, Soaked with blessings And imperishable wishes, The healing robe Granted the chance To live on, For someone discerned The mystery of prayer. Plenty of hints; Science teaches — Having shed its riddles, It keeps mixing medicines. The fleshly wars with the spiritual For the truth. But a kerchief or a ribbon, Or even a rag, Grants health To those full of faith.

93-9

If it wakes you in the night, It means it's truly important. Selected thoughts will Undermine The impossible. Yesterday's chaotic worries, Cleansed by sleep of silt, Will push you to work again, Will resurrect the past idea. Yesterday will continue tomorrow, More focused and stronger. And the cause — a perfected mantra, Hewn by a livelier word.

92-9

It's easy to trade A comrade for an enemy. But try the reverse: You'll quarrel with someone, Wait — though it's costly — For the enemy's hand of peace. Not to join him in crime, Nor drag him into yours. To grow stronger for now, Both you and him. To look into his eyes, Forget the insUlts, And in shared inspiration Leave the prison. The prison that with hAtred Is covered in mold, And the walls are coated With the frost of fury. And embracing in joy Under the dawn's glow, We'll head, unshackled, To the country of friendship.

91-7

Strong is the prayer Of the pickpocket thIEf, Ready to die In bloody battles. You can hear the prayer Of the tucked-up and tied-down, Unspoken aloud And unshed in thoughts. So why are you ashamed Of your own, In joy, in sorrow? The tomato prays. Isn't it time for you too?

90-9

The altruist loves — Seeks to serve. That's why he comes to knOw The joy of living. The sadist, the masochist Demands his Own. The egoist loves — Evil can't be avoided. To enslave others Is slavery for yourself (With more responsibility). Egoism is sacrilege.

89-9

She is his bone. Love calls To him ALone — Her pull toward the man. Her pull toward the man Is like the nature of glue; To stick to it — She needs care. That's what a woman is for — To keep him by her sIde. Her pull toward the man, For she yearns to rule over him.

88-4

They gain experience Through rich sacrifice. But in the end they mark The dOers of good as guilty. The indifferent — As if they'd never been — Made peace with the enemy. But a friend is no longer a friend — They quarreled with him. Who gave sincerely — From him more was asked. And who slowed the pace — At him they grew angry.

87-7

The Lord no longer accepts burnt offerings. Has He become a vegetarian, Or have mortals shed their delusions And the ritual of sacrifice fallen away? They've become gods unto themselves, Bringing praise to themselves; Satan rubs his hands — For Adam the frontier is already neAr. If there's no Creator, no sacrifices are needed either — Steal, rape, and lie. You'll have to die forEVER; Write off the sacrifice onto yourself.

86-7

As long as we don't stop Speaking the aggressor's language, The horde will persistently Not stop "liberating" us. It's wrong to stand out As a stranger among your own: As a Russian in Germany, As a German in Russia. Nor as a Muscovite in Ukraine With Cossack roots — In a forgotten generation, A rotten seed.

85-5

For those born in the sixties, Progress has yielded: From empty heavens To winged drones. From black-and-white television To accessible YouTube, Crude technology has developed. Dignity, alas, is lost. The achievements are great, Beyond words. But to the native word They never grew accustomed.

84-5

Which came first, the Hen or the egg? A rhetorical question. Sarmat or Pershing? This or that? — Lying is the orcs' habit. Of course "theirs is better, It's more advanced." "For it's harder on the enemy, For theirs hits harder." "They never even attacked, And there's truth on their side," "They were only defending" What's foreign, now theirs.

83-7

Don't fear different thinking; Allow yourself to argue. Since the start of reckoning, There'll never be found an End. We taste a hint of eternity. Since there is no end, Inflate it, though it will deflate — Not for yourself, for the Creator's glory. Not in vain are our souls' searches In the spiritual gyms of words, And the refusal to concede To the fraudsters' offers.

82-8

God is jealous toward traitors, Cruel toward the evil. He stops attackers, Strengthens the weak. He accepted sacrifices Until He sacrificed Himself; He abolished burnt offerings — He doesn't want what's dead. Neither dead love, Nor dead goodness, Nor cunning in the word, When the soul is dead.

81-9

Life is a scale, Effort is the rudder. Truth is fullness, Absence is zero. Movement — while you walk; Snagged — you're torn. You seek — you live. You've arrived — you're dead. The perfect is unattainable. Good is boundless. Evil will prove it. Learn — But carefully!!! Don't stumble.

80-9

You drive, not knowing Where it will strike. — You're playing with death, — It drills in your mind. Satan has arranged A safari on people; In his fervor he called Ukrainians Satan. At first glance He divided his kingdom. It will by no means StAnd. But what are doing here The Ukrainians' toll-houses? Separate them From the curses of henchmen.

79-9

Beneath the banners Of the грозный Savaof, Full of truth In God's words — The priest: Without an iron sword, But a spiritual sword In his lips. On the battlefield He'll do little — He won't hit the target, Won't down a plane. But in the rear he'll endow The army with love, He'll whiten anger at the aggressor, Pour grace onto conscience. So they'd love the country, Hate evil, Defend their own, Not surrender their Own.

78-8

The soul has shown itself. In a painting, in prose, in vERses. It used its own colors — Euphoria here, horror there. It captivated some, Irritated others, Left some indifferent, But declared: I am. I live. Reckon with me. I'll lay myself before you. I'll walk on dry land, Swim through water, Or fly through as a Spark.

77-9

You spent time — Gave away life. They paid you. Did it conscientiously, Cleaned everything up — Spent your strength. You live? What measures it? Money is the standard. Who are you? To verify, The background of finances will tell. Credit histories. Such is the earthly template. But answerable to heaven Is the overcoming Of obstacles in faith.

76-8

The hungry is no brother to the sated; The sated man's prayer Is insincere. The satiated has more holidays, For he's a grabber and a schemer. When someone has, he's a bourgeois — That's how the Bolsheviks taught. Judge him, spit at him, And hate with all your might. The American and the Jew Are to blame for everything (So the beggars think). They've saved up money — Now let them spend it.

75-9

Why is the father Distant from his children? Why is the mother In tears for them? She cares too much — A fur coat in the heat; For him, to strip to his underwear In icy cold. Dad understands his own way, Gives the children freedom. Mom warms with care, For her own is dEar to her. He lets go, yet holds on, And the child grows. He teaches to live — Both this and that.

74-7

To answer beautifully Doesn't have to be in verse. A message in prose Will serve no worse. You can say At least one word. And that's it — done. Nothing to add. Thank you. Dziękuję. Pięknie. Wonderful. Congratulations. Gratuluję. Noble. Honorowo.

73-6

With taxes They rob the population To fill with riches The "teremas of the heaven-dwellers." That's why the maidans Are in Zaporizhian genes — To tear off the shackles In corruption schemes. A tax service is needed For the people's good. Uncontrolled, it's misguided And causes harm.

72-9

Sodomy Destroys society. It prefers same-sexness Raised higher. It degenerates humanity, Advertises itself, Spreads debauchery, Ignores morality. You're gentle with it, But it grows brazen. It looks like a sprout, Dreaming of becoming a forest.

71-9

She wants — Quell your desires. Satisfy her. She wants — Hide your desires. They are hostile to her. She wants — Direct your desires To avoid war.

70-9

If you have no army — Invaders will come. An army Must be fed. Workers and farmers — True traitors When they rarely Agree to give. A powerful army — A temptation of aggression. Imperial ambitions, The regime's dictate. What is your power? Who are you, after all? With whom are YOUR coalitions? Only you can choose. You strive for peace, You will not kill, And your own soul You'll preserve above all. But you'll take the sharp axe From the storeroom — For those you love, You'll lay down your life.

69-9

The philosopher-poet Doesn't befriend wealth; The robber Won't rob him. From his sonnet Flows caring; A spit on affluence — He lives by the word alone. Immortality excites The thinker more. Diamonds and gold Don't glitter for him. He doesn't hear death; The eternal has converged in him — The vain, prostrate, He cannot accept. The romantic's delight Is not in hryvnias, not in euros. He constantly dreams Of how to save his soul. The Pacific, the Atlantic Will surely dry up When they learn how fervently He pursued his goal.

68-9

My bones already ache, Tired of lying down; Rested enough — Time to get up. Eagerly to work, To move mountains, Before I fall, Before grief befalls. But being ill is also a blessing. Thought works; In fog or thirstily It ponders eternity.

67-9

THERE was a word in the beginning With a good start. But we got used to it — It no longer sizzles. We put a period, Made it commonplace. Nothing is needed — It lies in the corner. It's covered in rust, Mold eats it away. And the tongue withers Without it. The essential has lived its life, And there's no strength — That's how a man perishes Without words. He says SOMEthing, Looks businesslike, Runs, walks, Writes something, makes noise. He thinks, creAtes, But knows no meaning. He'll fill the stove — But it won't burn.

66-9

NEw technologies ALways frighten. The unknown Disturbs, terrifies. Before childbirth They await pain; To DELIVER what is conceived — Hurts terribly. The too-high Threatens to fAll, The deep BeckONs into the abyss. The eye doesn't see — Fears to betray itself. The wide Hurries on a journey. To overcome distance, To know the new, To tear apart fears, To take what is hidden.

65-8

Sport for spectacles, For glory before people — To burn up your health, To shorten your life. A sacrifice of time and strength For medals on the chest. Someone needs it; For someone it's trash. To grow stronger in health, To drive away stress, To stir the body, cleanse the spirit — Don't torment yourself To raise your tone. What helps is not the race, but measured movement. The choice is yours — What do you lack? Vigor of spirit, or the hard labor of exercise? Sport may glorify, But it will surely destroy; Morning exercises, though humble, will preserve what you had.

64-9

The wisdom of chess — The boundlessness of variants. As in life — Go and figure it out. In its squares are treasures of talents. The moves are sIMple, But learn and learn. Only 6 pieces, 6 life statuses. In 6 days the Lord Created our world. The drill of ideas Works here too: Enter God In the format of a game. The law of life Is embedded in chess. It is encoded — Understand it yourself. Its squares — Bliss and horrors; Here you're either shackled Or rejoice.

63-8

You returned from captivity At the war's beginning — You're walking home, Where your wife and sons are. When they released you As the war flared up, Rejoice you weren't killed. But the meeting was sad. If it dragged on, You returned — and back to the ranks. Everyone turned away — Traitors, to battle.

62-6

Energy pours out Into the cup of eternity; From everyone it is expected To shed bitterness. Even in evil They seek betterness. If not for them, then for themselves — Greater worth. Eternity accepts From the living and the dead, From the whole and the ground-down. From whom it accepts, He draws from it.

61-9

Is time a line or a circle? How to count our days? A snowflake melts; you hear the word — They are the same, yet no longer the same. The war will pass, I thought; I said I wouldn't forgive the nit, For so much fury had gathered — And now I'm walking to meet it. Ready to extend my hand, And once more, in the cycle of all beginnings, I channel the forgotten Reincarnation.

60-9

Why do we need other Civilizations, If we need more Militarization? The time for star wars Has not yet come, For the atom to sweep away Billions together. But we learn eagerly — Bring on the cataclysms. What a celebration it'll be — Some to hell, some to heaven.

59-7

Saint Nicholas has returned. Enough of Grandfather Frost. Remember the sovok's mockery — A father's suffering asks for it. The commie thought To break the faith. Only a shadow of Christmas remains — But he won't strangle it. For some — Santa Claus, For some — Père Noël. Why did we ever need The godless "Myetyel"?

58-9

What have you done, Dmytro? You've changed the man. You changed his thinking; Peace has abandoned me. You've harnessed me to the phone — I only press the buttons. To what feats Do you call, unintentionally? I know, I know, it's not you. You only prayed. We're walking toward one goal — So that God may boast.

57-9

It tosses us around the world, With plans or without. Old, grown, children… He was in the village — then suddenly gone. Someone says: but how lucky. Others pity — it's hard there. Life has caught us like a whirlwind — Neither here nor there. There's no heroism in leaving, Nor in arriving either. Freedom becomes like a prison, But even in prison you don't cry.

56-7

I don't know if you believe in blessings, In your New Year's one in particular. But a new speaking has opened in me — Words keep coming out as verses. Hard to hold back the thoughts that matter; They tear toward freedom, hurry outward. Impatient, hot, swift, skittish. Where I laid them, they no longer lie. Sow yourself, grain — mAybe something will grow. They sowed in me — I've gathered into kernels. And maybe fate will reward me too? Maybe I'll lay down, where I took.

55-9

The "Russky mir" in all its "krasa": "We need to see How you all cry — Let everyone suffer." "That's their problem," they say, " God loves us, for we are holy. For the guilty will be tied up — We tie them, that's why we're tough." Blind "holy ones," blind killers, For grief is in others, not in them. The indifferent is Also a bloodsucker, In untruth Also lost, Also counted among the evil.

54-9

How is a poem born? Without inspiration — nothing at all. No spark, no light — darkness. It dwells in inspiration's wings. It will touch a thought with it in the ether, Send a barely audible wave, Line up the words in formation, Fold them into verses, into stanzas. Gone is gone, but when it coMES, Like a whirlwind, it will overTURN. All that is weak will become strong; From the strong it will make weak.

53-8

Both Shlyoma and Vanya, Both Jan and Jean, Sooner or later Life will ban. The sweetheart or the maniac, The tough guy or the nerd — Peacefully, or in fright, In a monastery or on the Titanic. They'll be lined up before the throne — As if all identical. Some will be written off, And some — Into the embrace of eternity.

52-8

Inspiration is like drinking beer with a gopnik In peaceful times. No inspiration — no miracle; Shout, run, or shake. But let the soul ignite With love or with anger at evil — It's enough to hurl a grenade Into the venomous serpent's nest. Dozens of orcs at once Inspiration will tear to shreds. It will destroy the ravenous infection And pave the way to life.

51-8

Tell yourself: it's lousy — And crap will crawl in from all sides. Proclaim: all is wonderful — Then await happy changes. The pleasure center is safe Thanks to encouraging words That guard its fortress, Keeping enemies away. The irritant from outside will lose its power If the gates are locked. Weakly the wings will flap, And the dragon will fly off.

50-7

White and black, Manifest and nonexistent, Sad and beneficent, Dead and seething. Mixed by relativity, Filled with shades. Where needed, unhurried, Somewhere accelerated. Squeezed between poles — DEPENDENCE ON ORBITS, Though bounded by edges, Doomed to boundlessness.

49-9

Absence and presence. Which of them is reality? Life and death — it is she too. She is — I am, I am not. Gave or stole, Refused or took, The idealist proposed, But the pessimist rejected. Saying he hadn't proved it — He deceived, he lied. Absence is also presence… That's why a lie is reality.

48-9

And in Russia there's another "bunt," For there are too many death notices; Coffins lie down in fresh soil. The dictator wages war. The people are outraged — "pazor!" In their intent to kill, Terror is too weak for them. They'd rather die. The "padyozh" of people is too small for them; The leader is forced to shout: "Ty kuda stranu vyodyosh? Where can I get wood for coffins?"

47-9

Weigh yourself in the evening and in the morning. The soul's weight is the difference. In you, her chosen one, She cannot sit still. When you sleep, She leaves your body. She flies somewhere while you lie, So the body may rest. She's cramped with you; Boundlessness is her element. To complete her mission quickly, To return to eternity — is her dream.

46-9

(The Beggar): "They stole from me, I stole from myself — It's called corruption. I came to you, And you lock yourself away." (The Rich Man): "I'm a good master, I didn't squander, That's why my barns are full. But you drool over what's not yours, To beg outside. What guarantee is there that if I give, You won't embezzle it? We'll believe your words — Then you'll receive."

45-9

Oh, how many geniuses Lie in cemeteries, Waiting for prizes In the heavens. Trampled by contemporaries, Ridiculed and tormented, Hanged and drowned, Yet honored by the Creator. They perished in hardship, Even their names are gone, "Cleaned up" and forgotten… We follow THEM.

44-8

Infectious trash The Master of life Added to the air. He sent a pandemic — A violation of measure, The destroying angel, A test of faith For every inhabitant. Will they discern where the fictions are — Human or of gods? Will they run to the doctor, Or to the Doctor of doctors?

43-8

Above all, Care for your heart, For it carries The soul — your very first. Under the gravestone It will be buried. Where is it? They won't even recall. But as the vessel The incense leaves, So the heart frees The labor-worn soul.

42-8

Your video greeting card I'm seeing for the third time. I had hoped that, tipsy, You'd add something of your own. A piece of heart and soul Is what the owner's word gives. Whether prose or verse — Only let it be your own. The artificial is dead, A copy is a corpse. A living sacrifice — In communion, a marriage.

41-7

When you warm your chest With blankets on the sheet, A cold — Is also a blessing in the Lord. And on weekends, On New Year's night, There comes in a dream Quite a thing. You pick up the phone And write in VERses — A marathon of thoughts You'll leave even for others.

40-6

Essence matters, Intuition will choose the style. Words flow from within, Bypassing rust and rot. Iamb or trochee, Freestyle or canon — Primitive for people. No obstacles. The soul was tearing free — I didn't hold the door. It didn't care — Iamb or trochee.

39-7

They seek treasures and gold — Bliss, glory — here it is! But they don't notice the hammer of sins, Its treachery. Having chosen mammon* through wealth, Having driven out God and morality, Will we truly return Home, Will we hold the Grail?** Wish for money and riches, Health, happiness, and good — But beware of sacrilege, Lest the soul perish. * mammon — profit, gain ** grail — the sacred golden cup that held the Savior's blood as it flowed from the cross

38-9

In prayer we ask — And break God's plans. We bring thanks — However we vote, We compel Him to nothing. "Thy will be done" — We say in the Our Father. There is no "I" of ours — Instead of doing, we'll lie down. It is a sin to shirk cooperation, Knowing the Lord's intentions; Cooperation is necessary — Reaching the goal together with Him,

37-8

Nothing is eternal — It appeared and vanished. Summer raged — and winter. You can't bring it back — a pity. Days, months, and seasons Settle as silt into the well of time. But having waited their turn, They circle in repetition, For they rise again. They have no end, Though they die… …Do you hear God's call?

36-9

The Prince of Peace is born — Bayonets down. The drone has stopped, Turned back home. For even a day, the faithful Will not kill, will not rape. Will remember he's peaceful — Once a year, he'll crack a joke. Christ was born To die gloriously… …So the soldier crossed himself In the embrace of death.

35-9

Fewer flags — We've grown tired. Indifference is the first To flee from the groans. We're sick of depression, We want victories. Aggression is forgotten — Enough of alarms. The neighbor's house Is already burning out. But I must plow — The field is waiting.

34-9

Time to move the capital, For Kyiv has suddenly vanished somewhere. Ukrainian doesn't suit him — Now the tongue rules here. Vinnytsia and Khmelnytskyi rejoice — The tongue has shrunk the country; They'll take over Ukraine. For a rapist has entered Kyiv. The Moscow Kyiv Governorate — The rocket and bayonet did their best. From Azovsk to Lviv marches The Ukrainsky russky yazyk.

33-6

8 rockets… What poems now. No time for sonnets — We have it worst. If only to survive, To hide. What is there to strut about, Or to boast? Like dominoes we line up, They bombed us in the morning — We fold into verses Across the ocean.

32-8

Everyone takes up a mission To serve God and the people. Kindly or spitefully, Hoping for a reward. Whether he loves or hAtes — He counts himself righteous. See, his arrow flies — He looses it with love. Good and evil have Polarity. Their charges swap. He's loved his fill, and anger again — While the stars smile.

31-9

On my knees I'll surely survive, On my feet I may walk through. If they don't drive me out, They'll bury me when I die. To crawl the earth as a worm, To fly the heavens as an eagle. To glide the water as a boat, As a turtle, to merge with the bottom. The honest does not drown in streams, The just does not burn in fire. Abel is going home; Cain will pay for it ALL.

30-9

To stoke the fire When it's blazing? Or to rejoice in THAT Which vanishes in it? We say "good" When we take. "Evil" — When we give. Serve your neighbor — Prepare to burn. Show the Almighty How you can warm.

29-7

I see it now: To say a museum will buy it Is too little. The painting speaks to all people, Universally. Dignity in the face, A soul in the breast. It breathes lightness — Byssus, not brocade. Yellow-and-blue Came the inspiration. "Unshakable Ukrainian" Is the beauty's name.

28-7

Born to suffer, To learn to give thanks. So I will love Instead of mourning. Thank you for blessings, Thank you for poverty. For someone's respect, For sneering grimaces. For beatings and for cures With love as their mark I must rejoice. Thank you, God, thank you.

27-9

People flee from grief, Avoid calamity — Seeking shelter. From mountain to mountain They crawl and fly, From sea to sea. Among a foreign people, They dress in feathers — Hoping later to fleece Their sponsors. Be Abel — Help your brother. With axe and stone — Against your own executioner.

26-9

You see but dimly. You never know Where you will lose And where you will meet. You met him as a friend — He became an enemy. Mockery seized you — God granted a little happiness. Submissive to fate, Ready for anything. He will rejoice in freedom, But will endure slavery too.

25-8

Wonderful weather, Butterflies flutter. Nature rejoices, Troubles flee. The ostrich has hidden Its head in the sand. The chimp has put Its mouth under lock. I hear nothing, No stink of shit — I propose: "Davaytye spayom."

24-5

If our language didn't teach us humanity, Maybe the tongue will? Let chaff feed us From screens, speakers, and books. The language will become needless, We'll speak with the tongue. By the power of the russkava slova We'll take Prague and London, vazmyom! We'll forget all that's Ukrainian, Renounce our parents. We'll swell the orc army — To kill brothers for the language.

23-6

Rhymes visit from happiness, And in grief a verse asks to be born. The muse dispels misfortunes So they don't turn for the worse. The artist paints pictures, The shepherd tends his flocks. To create is the calling of man, Who carries a torch of light. Dawn peeks through the little window — Let's say "enough" to the darkness. Let us believe in tomorrow's sun — An end will come to the war as well.

22-9

We paint little huts, Don embroidered shirts, Long for the village, Lie down in the rye. We love Ukraine And her guelder-rose; We quarrel among ourselves To the point of ruin. Ready to perish Again and again, To soar to the stars — Just not for the language.

21-4

We do not war, you and I — Others are drafted into the ranks. They are sent into battle; THEY bear the true service. We hide from the draft officer, Or maybe came for an appointment — The young are ordered to die, To grow stronger in the breach. Inexperienced, but nimble, Better at the front line. The front in the rear matters too — If not yours and not theirs, then mine.

20-7

Army, language, faith (Mogilizatsiya, Putin, yazyk). Though the skin stayed the same, He's unlearned how to be human. Only in the village — a Ukrainian, But in the city — I'm a Russky muzhik. From the capital, from Donetsk, from Vinnytsia lands Comes the russky yazyk. There the Petrovs are cool guys, And I'm among them, like a bull. We crave slavery and blood — That's what the rasyeisky yazyk does.

19-7

They'll check your health, whether you're fit, Hand you a summons to muster, Let your family see you off, Stamp the papers with a seal. Bandits and hooligans, Drunks and junkies, The romantic and the expert Await on the field of battle — The best and the worst dregs. Nature cleanses itself; The evil stored up in the world Thirsts to drink blood... War… — that's exactly it.

18-7

Keep pestering, Keep drawing in, Keep praising, Keep holding. Lest you forget, Lest you be forgotten. Lest you abandon, Lest you be abandoned. Write, call, speak. Remind them you remember. Wait and reply — Then they hold you… and you hold.

17-7

In memory There is a peculiar property: The crumpled Loses its vividness. The distanced Disappears. The praised Attracts. The unmoving Is forgotten. The tiresome Remains.

16-9

Doves, doves, No cats. Live and love — Peace, quiet. Cats, cats, And not a single dove. They won't let you pass, Meowing from hunger. Cats and doves, Commotion. Time of struggle… …for Putin to croak!

15-6

They don't love us, for we're cattle, Perverts and butchers. They obviously fear us, For such are fathers and grandfathers. We've soiled our way across the planet, And through years-centuries, On TV, in the papers: "We can repeat it!" They repeat it, strangely enough. Evil sits in the chromosomes. They feel no shame, no disgrace — "They can repeat it!"

14-9

We sympathize with your grief From the blasts of "brotherly" rockets. From the air, from land, and from sea Russia sends you "privyet." Her love is boundless, Ready to strangle. Lying and hypocritical, She rapes. She craves to kill. She smashes cities and villages, Destroys all that lives, And broods, joyless — Why don't they love her?

13-8

To love Russian — Is to live in Russia. To count yourself Ukrainian — Is to speak Ukrainian. Switch to what's foreign — And the foreign will take you. As if you were — But who, you've forgotten. The language is gone — Ukraine has fallen. What then did we fight for, Shed blood for?

12-7

A slightly fascist philosophy, Cruel, and harsh to the ear. Maybe crude, dumb, and peasant-like — It will surely outrage someone's spirit. You can't hide your eyes from the truth; It will get in behind your eyelids. ONE WAY OR ANOTHER YOU DIE — And where will the soul end up? Conscience will call you to the trenches, Or fling you across the ocean. My proposal: interrogate yourself — Did you choose truth, or deception?

11-7

People the earth, Succeed your fathers. Shine where it is dark, Where no banners fly. I will go before you, I will pave your ways, With your heels You shall crush the serpent. I could do it Myself. But in Glory I grant it to you as well. You and I — We walk as a pair.

10-7

I still cannot grasp How one can Love Ukraine — Yet drown it in Russian, "With feelings deep." What kind of Ukrainian is that, With a katsap's tongue? Who will replace for him Mother, father, brother? However improper, "What difference does it make," he'll say Of what is foreign, nay hostile — And lie down under the oppressor?

9-7

What is he feeding his ears? It would sicken me. Rage would tear me apart — Contempt for the evil. I have grown allergic To propagandists. One hope remains — No more rashists. No health left To drink their slop. If only the war would fade — I want to live.

8-6

Who is the co-author? The one who inspires. But him Few know. It began as a joke — Trading verses in letters — A renewed start In the game of words. Let me remind you: I am not alone. As a troubadour, Even Yura will do.

7-7

A lion has seized The innocent by the throat. None dare to rescue — The roar frightens. Two sharp horns Has each of them. Yet it is not so simple To find one able To stand against the villain, To free the victim from death, To brave his own peril — To take her place himself.

6-7

This truth is not for everyone — Unfitting. Like a sin, Very private. Subconsciously everyone Carries it around. Out of fright Begs to live. Let it be someone else — Why me? Though I am sinful, I have preserved life.

5-7

To exist on your knees as a slave — The free are carried on wings. For freedom they go to die — They die, yet they live. On your knees you take the yoke — Not killed, but do you live? You push your people into bondage, For you walk into it first. On your knees you surrender to man, To serve the eternal evil. Unless you fight for truth — On my knees I go to God.

4-7

Can anyone still believe That we are guilty? Russia kills us Because it forbids us To war against it. Someone will lie down under the thief. "Think nothing of it," he'll say, "What difference does it make? We'd switch to Russian. I'll speak it myself. I'd trade Ukrainian For their song. As a servant, as a slave, With a bowed head — But I'll live." It came to "liberate." To destroy and to take. Such is its love For orphans and widows.

3-7

Archangel Michael Is in Ukraine NOW, Nine months already. In the east and in the south He chases Putin's horde. I won't say he is Zaluzhny, But he is Zaluzhny's commander. He makes Ukrainians courageous, And the horde's plan a failure. Zhora-George Is searing, Michael swings his sword, Palageya is blazing. They war with heavenly fire.

2-7

Nostalgia of memory — The sovok holds fast. Locked into the past, They lunged forward. The old have lost their way — The children will find it. Hopes are shattered — The grandchildren will gather them. We sigh for what is lost — Laughter to the young. We weep. They are merry.

1-7
